From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Reserved capacity options and lane-slice ramp playbook — Sawtooth Bio

Hi Emma / Jacob,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — really appreciated the walk-through of Sawtooth's ingestion profile and expected traffic spikes during batch validation. I've attached a concise options pack (sawtooth-reserve-options-v1.pdf) with three reservation structures that map to different operational risk profiles. High level:

- Option A — Lane Slice (conservative onramp): 12 min GPUs anchored in us-west, supports steady production load. Cluster: 12 GPUs (H100 logical lanes), warm cache pool 1.5x baseline, prewarm credits: 1 week. Ramp: 12 -> 24 at month 3 based on 90th percentile token throughput trigger.
- Option B — Stepped Tranche (recommended for growth): 12 min GPUs, stepped to 36 GPUs over 3 tranches (months 1, 3, 6). Each tranche activates automatically when 95th percentile sustained usage exceeds tranche threshold for two consecutive weeks. Includes burst buffer and model-fallback lanes.
- Option C — Anchored Slate (predictable throughput, lower latency SLO): 32 min GPUs with phased decommit windows and higher SLA; suited if you want consistent tail latency during peak experiments.

Pricing and SLA tradeoffs are in the attached doc. A couple of notes specific to Sawtooth's profile:
- We recommend keeping the minimum reserve at 12 GPUs rather than 8 given your multi-model ensemble and KV cache requirements — that materially reduces cold-start pressure.
- Autoscaling burst credits are available for experimental windows; we can allocate a 10% onboarding credit in month 1 if you prefer a soft-start.

Ask: can you confirm which option feels closest to your risk/cost appetite? If you want, I can draft a hybrid tranche (12 -> 48 over six months) and run an estimated burn model.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm option by EOD Tue 11 Aug
2) We prepare a formal Reserve Purchase Order + DocuSign, including warm-start credits and activation-triggers
3) Karthik to validate warm-cache sizing and prewarm window for us-west region

Thanks — attaching the options pack.

—
Marissa Cole
Principal AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0176

Emma — thanks, great questions. I sketched a hybrid that meets your 12-GPU floor and gives a predictable activation runway while staying cost-conscious. Key changes (attached pricing spreadsheet):

Hybrid Stepped Plan (custom):
- Minimum anchor: 12 GPUs (us-west) — baseline for your ensemble and KV cache.
- Tranche 1: immediate activation to 12 GPUs + 2 weeks of warm-cache prefill.
- Tranche 2: month 2 -> automatic add of 12 GPUs (total 24) if 95th percentile sustained token throughput > X for 14 days.
- Tranche 3: month 4 -> add 24 GPUs (total 48) if usage continues to exceed tranche threshold.
- Decommit windows: 30-day minimum on any decommit; decommit requires both sustained drop and notice window.
- Warm-start / burst credits: we can apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of month 1 committed spend (applied as credits over months 1–3) for the POC.

Operational/fallback guidance:
- For early ramp, we recommend enabling KV cache warm pool (1.5x baseline) and keeping a 2-GPU hot buffer for traffic spikes to avoid tail-latency regressions.
- If you expect cross-region DR, we can reserve a small cold standby in us-east with async failover; that would be priced separately.

Next steps:
- If you approve the hybrid plan I will: 1) finalize spare-capacity runbook with Karthik, 2) produce DocuSign MOA with the onboarding credit and tranche activation logic, and 3) set a tentative activation date.

I've attached the updated pricing workbook: sawtooth-reserve-pricing-080726.xlsx

—
Marissa

Quick tech note for the runbook Marissa will finalize:

- GPU spec: recommend H100 80GB profiles for the ensemble runs; if Sawtooth prefers A100 80GB we can model latency differences but H100 gives better quantization headroom.
- Warm cache / KV sizing: plan for a warm-cache pool sized at ~1.5x your 95th percentile token footprint to keep the KV hit-rate high during tranche activations. That reduces cold-start token penalty by ~60%.
- Autoscaling: use a throughput-aligned policy (token/sec) with two trigger bands: tranche activation (sustained 14 days) and burst scaling (short-term 10–15 minute windows up to reserved+burst).
- Observability: instrument per-route p95 token latency dashboards and token-burn alerts that push to your PagerDuty channel. We recommend setting initial p95 target at 250–350ms for ensemble inference — adjust after POC.

I'll sync with Marissa on final warmup windows and binary warm-fill runbooks.

—Karthik
